newsitem.title: USA: Farmers begin harvesting corn in U.S. Delta states.
newsitem.headline: Farmers begin harvesting corn in U.S. Delta states.

text.p: Farmers in southern Louisana and Mississippi have begun to harvest some early yielding varieties of corn, cash merchandisers and crop observers said.
"There's plenty of corn being harvested here," said David Bollich, grain marketing specialist with the Louisiana Farm Bureau.
Bollich said that approximately 20 percent of the state's crop had been harvested, and early quality reports were favorable.
Early corn yields in Louisiana ranged from 125 to 160 bushels per acre, he said.
On Monday, the Louisiana Agricultural Statistics Service said eight percent of the state's crop had been harvested. That figure is equal with the five-year average.
Cash grain dealers in Mississippi said farmers were also beginning to harvest corn in the far southern parts of the state.
"They got their first load of corn from Mississippi in Memphis yesterday (Monday)," said one river dealer.
However, another cash grain dealer in north-central Mississippi said corn harvest in her area was still two weeks away.
On Monday, the Mississippi Agricultural Statistics Service said 20 percent of the corn crop was mature during the week ended Sunday, but no harvest progress was reported.
Farmers in central and southern Texas also harvested corn last week.
According to the state's weekly crop progress report, six percent of the crop was harvested versus the five-year average of 20 percent.
